findings.rule: .claude/skills/code-review/SKILL.md#10 Predicate sweep — "**For each**, write two things — the rule it is there to enforce, and the exact question the code asks. **Blocks when those are not the same question.** ... the invariant spans two facts and the write constrains one of them"
findings.claim: The commit split one write into two phases — an intent at cmdResume:620 and a commit at route():266-269 — and wrote only the setting half. `if (replans && sha !== run.specSha) run.pendingSpecSha = sha;` asks "did the spec on disk move away from the recorded sha", but the rule the field has to hold is "pendingSpecSha is the sha the next replan will compile handoff.json from". Those stop being the same question the moment a pending value already exists and this resume's predicate is false: nothing clears it, so a stale intent survives and route():267 later stamps it onto run.specSha as the provenance of a plan that was compiled from something else. It is the mirror image of the defect it fixed — pass 3's finding was an intent recorded too early, this is an intent that never expires.

witness.detail: run.specSha=S0; the run halts at review with a spec-defect finding. (1) The person edits specs/requests/01-requests.md S0->S1, commits, and runs `wf resume --stage pre_implement --accept-spec-edits`: wf.mjs:620 sets run.pendingSpecSha=S1 and leaves run.specSha=S0. (2) The pre-implementer runs and itself reports a spec blocker — pre_implement's authority includes 'spec' (wf.mjs:61) — so route() halts the run with 'spec-defect' and :266 never fires; pendingSpecSha=S1 persists in run.json. (3) The person accepts that the S1 edit was wrong, reverts the spec commit so the file is byte-identical to S0 again, and runs `wf resume --stage pre_implement --accept-spec-edits`. Now :578 computes sha=S0, and :620's predicate `sha !== run.specSha` is S0 !== S0 = false, so pendingSpecSha is neither set nor cleared: it stays S1. :626 records specSha {from:S0, pendingUntilReplan:S1} for a resume that moved nothing. (4) The pre-implementer compiles handoff.json from the spec on disk, S0, and passes; route():266-269 fires and sets run.specSha=S1, deleting pendingSpecSha. Wrong observable result: run.json now says the plan was compiled from S1 while both handoff.json and the spec on disk are S0, and every later `wf resume --stage implement|review|qa` is refused at :579-584 with "specs/requests/01-requests.md changed since this run was planned, so handoff.json describes a spec that no longer exists" — which is false, handoff.json describes exactly the spec on disk. `wf preflight`'s spec-unchanged check at :471 fails against an unchanged spec for the same reason. That permanent unresumability behind a false message is the precise failure the comment at :615-618 says this code exists to prevent.

findings.suggestedFix: Drop the two-phase write rather than patching its second half: delete the pendingSpecSha field and have route() read the truth at the moment the plan is known to be rebuilt — in the pre_implement pass branch, `run.specSha = sha256(readFileSync(resolve(ROOT, run.spec), 'utf8'))`. That is unconditionally the sha the pre-implementer just compiled from and has no stale-state class at all. If the field is kept, :620 must invalidate as well as set — `if (replans) { if (sha !== run.specSha) run.pendingSpecSha = sha; else delete run.pendingSpecSha; }` — and :626 must record the value this call wrote rather than whatever happens to be on the object.
